policy: The debate text is authored synthesis/paraphrase unless an individually attributed literal quotation has been independently verified.
Every debate has a linked source from the actual opposing literature or contemporary institutional position; this DOES NOT alone verify each eight-stage paraphrase.
Opposing claims and Catholic rebuttals require independent provenance; the position-source registry and question moral sources are not interchangeable.
Book catalogue pages are bibliographic leads only, not proof of an exact position on a specific page.
High-impact clinical descriptions require the relevant original clinical guideline rather than a generic organizational policy page.
Do not mark audit complete until all 55 debate positions and eight stages have source-level editorial review.

details.findings: The Tablet explains Fletcher's love and situational norm. The precise question is an editorial reconstruction, not Fletcher's exact quotation or all Christian approaches to intention.

The Tablet documents situation ethics' priority of love over absolute rules. A claim that ANY act is justified in ANY exception overstates Fletcher and must be treated as a test objection, not a literal position.
Freud's 1908 essay directly criticizes repression and deferred sexual expression. It neither examines Catholic chastity as a freely chosen virtue nor proves such virtue intrinsically pathological.

Isacco et al. report several priests' first-person loneliness and depression experiences; 6 of 15 interviewees mention negative effects. This is not proof that lifelong freely chosen celibacy necessarily damages mental health.

Pew 2019 documents cohabiters' own reasons, including testing a relationship (23% major reason), finances (38%), and convenience (37%). It does not conclude premarital cohabitation improves marriage stability.

Neither Planned Parenthood's general sexual health page nor Farley's book catalogue documents 'looking is not touching' as a moral doctrine. Farley has been removed as purported support. This remains a hypothetical common retort; no invented proponent.
Pew respondents name love and companionship among marriage motives. It does not conclude the procreative end is obsolete; the contrast is an authored challenge, not an attributed Pew claim.

Francis' original Spadaro interview criticizes disproportionate repetition of abortion/contraception/marriage issues and calls for a broader Gospel setting; he does not renounce Catholic sexual ethics or say its norms are false.

Freud's original 1908 critique of sexual restraint is a historical position, not evidence that twenty-first-century dating, pornography and delayed marriage make chastity impossible; the modern impossibility premise remains hypothetical.

Gray & Klement 2026 report correlation of purity-culture exposure with sexual shame in 1,273 respondents but explicitly no causal proof. Other 2026 trauma-group study concerns evangelical purity culture, not Catholic doctrine generally. Neither refutes Catholic chastity by itself.

The Tablet accurately summarizes Fletcher's agape and six propositions, but 'love is love' as any attraction justifies sexual relations is not Fletcher's stated wording. Ethical agape and mere attraction must be distinguished.

editorial_cautions: Secondary accounts of Joseph Fletcher's situation ethics are NOT firsthand Fletcher quotations.
Freud critiques sexual abstinence in 1908, not the developed virtue theology of Catholic chastity.
Pew reports respondents' motivations, not a moral norm or causal marriage-outcome finding.
Priest interview and purity-culture studies are small/observational context and cannot establish universal psychological necessity.
Sexual shame studies concern particular evangelical purity-culture messaging and may not be generalized causally to Catholic doctrine.
CSE038 is an illustrative retort with no discovered individual author/proponent; readers are warned rather than provided a made-up opponent.
Prior book-preview references remain bibliographic context, not specific-page certification.
